thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PD alert fired: prom-exporter-heartbeat-missing (P1)

incident-bot: auto-escalation -> sre-oncall -> ops-lead (unacked for 2m)

sre-oncall: on it. seeing a spike of 500+ scrape failures across eu-west that started ~2m ago.

maria: which exporters? all node-exporters or specific app exporters?

aj: looks like kubelet and node-exporter primarily. some apm-exporter 503s too.

ops-lead: any recent deploys to eu-west?

maria: not from our side. infra deploys show nothing in the last 30m.

sre-oncall: grabbing logs from scrape-proxy. tail:```
level=warn ts=2024-11-03T14:35:10Z msg=\"scrape failed\" job=kubelet target=10.2.8.12 error=\"dial tcp 10.2.8.12:10250: connect: connection refused\"
```

aj: that connect refused is weird — kubelets should be healthy. Could be network route flap or iptables churn.

ops-lead: PD note: customer-impact? dashboards showing gaps?

sre-oncall: Grafana shows missing kubelet metrics for ~40% of hosts in eu-west cluster-prod. Alerting for dashboards is triggering customer-ops ticket.

cs-rep: I'm getting incoming slack pings from a customer saying their monitoring alerts fired. Flagging them for impact comms.

maria: quick mitigation: can we stop scraping the failing targets to allow backlog to drain? alternatively switch to fallback metrics aggregated stream.

aj: stopping scrapes will reduce immediate error noise but won't stop PD from paging if rules are tied to absence. We can mute the PD rule temporarily (manual suppress) while we mitigate.

ops-lead: agree. I'll mute the prom-exporter-heartbeat-missing alert for eu-west for 15m. tagging with: \"muted-by:ops-lead - investigating network/e2e\"

incident-bot: @ops-lead muted alert prom-exporter-heartbeat-missing (eu-west) for 15m

sre-oncall: running quick health checks to determine if it's kube-proxy or network fabric. curl from scrape-proxy to 10.2.8.12:```
> curl -v http://10.2.8.12:10250/metrics
*   Trying 10.2.8.12...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* connect to 10.2.8.12 port 10250 failed: Connection refused
* Failed to connect to 10.2.8.12 port 10250: Connection refused
```

aj: same from another host in eu-west. However, ping/ICMP responds. That suggests kubelet process may have crashed or is refusing connections.

maria: can we check kubelet logs via k8s master?

sre-oncall: running `kubectl get nodes --selector=region=eu-west -o wide` then `kubectl logs -n kube-system kubelet-<node>` - but if kubelet died we may not be able to retrieve logs.

incident-bot: PD update: incident acknowledged by sre-oncall (P1)

ops-lead: meanwhile, scale up the consumer pool for the metrics ingest so backlog doesn't hit storage limits. aj please spin +4 consumers in eu-west metrics-consumer autoscale group.

aj: doing that now. CLI: `aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name eu-metrics-consumers --desired-capacity 12`

aj: started 4 new instances, joining consumer set. Lag monitoring shows backlog ingestion rate improving ~30s after join.

maria: I'm seeing a correlated spike in conntrack table size on the scrape-proxies: conntrack entries ~ 250k -> 800k, kernel dropping new conns. Could explain connection refuses.

sre-oncall: nice find. can we flush conntrack or rotate proxies? prefer graceful: drain one scrape-proxy at a time and replace.

ops-lead: approve. aj rotate scrape-proxy-eu-1 -> drain, terminate, let ASG replace. then monitor conntrack.

aj: draining scrape-proxy-eu-1: `kubectl cordon scrape-proxy-eu-1 && kubectl drain scrape-proxy-eu-1 --ignore-daemonsets` then terminate instance.

aj: terminated; new instance booting. conntrack usage dropped ~45s after drain. kubelet connections starting to succeed again.

maria: kubelet responses are back for ~60% of nodes now. prometheus scrape success rate climbing.

sre-oncall: removing manual mute on PD? I recommend keep mute for another 5m while we validate stable.

ops-lead: leaving the mute for 5m. add a note: "muted until stable, root cause suspected conntrack exhaustion on scrape-proxies"

incident-bot: @ops-lead extended mute for 5m

cs-rep: told customer CS that we saw a regional scraping disruption, investigating, and dashboards may have gaps for ~10-20m. they'll escalate if they need more.

maria: follow-up actions: 1) add conntrack monitoring + alert at 75% of capacity for scrape-proxies 2) increase ephemeral conntrack table on proxies as stopgap 3) improve autoscaling policy to pre-warm consumers when scrape errors spike 4) run a postmortem.

aj: creating task cards: `ENGSRE-8421 increase conntrack and add alert` and `ENGSRE-8422 consumer prewarm`

sre-oncall: marking incident resolved in PD after metrics stable for 10m.

incident-bot: PD status changed -> resolved by sre-oncall (P1)

ops-lead: good work. please include ingestion lag numbers and exact timestamps in the postmortem. also include customer impact notes from CS.

maria: will do. saving logs and graphs to the incident folder: `s3://redwood-incidents/3456789012/`

aj: leaving one follow-up: run a small chaos test for conntrack pressure in staging to validate hardening.

sre-oncall: thanks team. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
